problems.source_says: The manuscript explicitly introduces overall enjoyment as a measure of the quality of each story. Section 6 of the supplied codebook places quality of a single output under usefulness. Coding this stated quality measure as other therefore does not follow the construct definition; the appropriate code is usefulness. Its external rating, with_ai question, and participant-level analysis remain supported.
problems.quote: To assess the quality of each story, we included an overall enjoyment rating from raters
problems.locator: PDF p. 17, Experiment 1, Measures, Creativity measure, paragraph beginning "To assess the quality"; creativity-codebook.md, section 6, Construct table, usefulness definition.

problems.source_says: The manuscript reports embedding similarity of creative products and greater similarity among AI-assisted outputs, but never defines the comparison pool or establishes that the compared outputs are from different participants. Experiment 2 retained 329 works from 299 participants, including multiple works from some participants. The required between-person basis for diversity, and thus across_people, remains unconfirmed. The form acknowledges the missing comparison pool but nevertheless assigns both codes definitively. The correct classification cannot be confirmed from the saved PDF; no replacement construct is inferred. The cited online appendices are absent, and attempts to retrieve the linked OSF materials through its API and webpage failed with WinError 10013.
problems.quote: Second, we again assessed the similarity of the creative products using textual analysis techniques (embedding).
problems.locator: PDF pp. 28-29, Experiment 2, Supplementary Analysis, second analysis; pp. 23-24, multiple lyric submissions and 329 works from 299 participants; creativity-codebook.md, sections 1 and 6 (diversity must compare different people). summary: Criterion 3 holds, and the reported outcome numbers match the saved PDF. The coding is refuted because S1-O3 describes story quality but codes it as other, while S2-O7 lacks explicit support for a between-person diversity/across_people classification.
